chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Abu al-Mi'za said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was with him, saying: 'May God perfect you, I pass by the tax collector and he approves/validates for me with the dirhams, do I take them?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'And do I perform Hajj with them?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.اَلْعَامِلُ: The tax collector or state official

ai.seo_question: Can money received from the government or tax collector be used for Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of using funds received from the state treasury or tax collectors, affirming that such dirhams are considered pure (halal) for personal consumption and valid for fulfilling religious obligations like Hajj. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that the source of income from legitimate state authorities does not inherently invalidate its spiritual utility, provided the transaction itself is not explicitly corrupt. It serves as a practical legal precedent for believers navigating economic interactions with governing powers in Islamic society.
